body: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. filed a mortgage foreclosure suit on March 27, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois against 181 West Madison Property LLC, owner of the 50-story office tower at 181 West Madison Street in the Chicago Loop. The case is assigned to Judge Robert W. Gettleman. According to The Real Deal, the loan is $240 million, the suit was brought through the loan's special servicer, Situs, and more than $223 million is due.

The Real Deal reported that the borrower is wholly owned by SinOceanic I Limited, a Bermuda company that became the owner in 2023 through the bankruptcy of the previous landlord, China's HNA Group. The publication tied the March default to Northern Trust, the building's longtime anchor tenant, which cut its lease from 400,000 to 225,000 square feet starting this year, with a period of free rent, leaving the owner short of what it needed for debt service and reserves.

On April 3, Wells Fargo asked the court to appoint Matthew Mason of Hilco Real Estate as receiver. The receivership motion, as described by The Real Deal, says utility bills and some vendors were going unpaid and that without a receiver the property faced an "imminent danger" of damage or loss of value. The court gave the borrower until April 22 to respond. The borrower filed no response and did not appear, and Chief Judge Virginia M. Kendall granted the motion on April 23 and signed the order appointing the receiver on April 24.

Wells Fargo then moved for a default, and on June 14 the court entered an order of default against 181 West Madison Property LLC. The docket shows status filings and an extension of time through Aug. 31, 2026.

timeline.label: SinOceanic I Limited becomes owner through HNA Group's bankruptcy
Wells Fargo files federal foreclosure suit
Motion to appoint Hilco's Matthew Mason as receiver
Court appoints receiver after the borrower fails to respond
Court enters order of default against the borrower
